interpretation: Aristotle notes that some things are the same both potentially and actually, 'not at the same time, or not in the same respect' (ουχ αμα δε η ου κατα το αυτο), e.g. actually hot and potentially cold. Read as the principle that whatever is both is never so at once in one respect, which is Aquinas' non-simultaneity premise; the hot/cold example is the one Aquinas uses. The clause qualifies 'some things are both', so the universal reading is the step this claim takes; Aristotle uses it at once to explain why physical movers are acted on, not to argue for a first mover. No time index is formalized: the Lean premise is read at one time, as in the prima via.
